n01: The garden is hers, not mine. I don't like snails.
n02: She names flowers; I forget them, the flowers don't.
n03: He's learning to speak; quiet like the plants. Crossed-out mistake.
n04: Migas uses the little hedge door, eats our bread, no sorry.
n05: Evening walk; she jumps the stile, now brambles cover it.
n06: Her low wooden chair; she blames my knees. It's hers.
n07: My first perfect long sentence, said to the neighbour's dog.
n08: From the hill at midnight, a yellow light that never goes out.
n09: The far light: someone I fell out with, eleven winters ago.
p1: Snail on my stool again; she still says that's no reason.
d1: She brings coffee up to the hill; still doesn't ask.
p2: Wind on the hill; I said nothing.
d2: This time she brings coffee, something for wind, and stays.
p3: Now she says my stool is too low.
d3: I bring my own coffee now. Nobody asks. She's gone?
n10: I watered your side of the garden too.
n11: Her cup stays empty; I give it to Migas. Talking to snails.
p4: I signalled once to the far light. Nobody answered.
n12: Two signals; the far light answered with two.
n13: Now the garden is yours: water, Migas, two signals, snails.

n01: The garden is hers, not mine. Bench for two, stool for one.
n02: She names flowers; I forget them, the flower doesn't.
n03: All day in the garden; plants don't talk, me neither yet.
n04: Migas uses the little hedge door, eats bread, never says sorry.
n05: Evening walks; she jumps the stile, now brambles cover it.
n06: Her low wooden chair; she blames my knees, not the chair.
n07: My first perfect long sentence, said to the neighbour's dog; she laughed.
n08: From the hill at midnight, a yellow light that never goes out.
n09: Far light: an old quarrel, eleven winters; no courage to say sorry.
p1: Snail on my stool again; she still says that's no reason.
d1: Tonight she brings me coffee at the far light, never asking.
p2: Wind on the hill; I said nothing.
d2: Coffee and something for the wind; this time she stays.
p3: Now she says my stool is too low. Roles swapped.
d3: I bring my own coffee now. She's gone, I think.
n10: I watered your side of the garden too. She's dead.
n11: Her empty cup goes to Migas; I talk to Rayo the snail.
p4: I flashed a light signal once to the far light. No answer.
n12: Two signals, and the far light answered with two.
n13: The garden is mine now: water, Migas, two signals. Snails no reason.
